subject: Clarify: default storage windows for requests vs generated outputs
messages:
From: Alice Wong <alice@brightlane.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: security@brightlane.com
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarify default storage for requests/outputs (EU)

Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking time to help — we're doing a security review ahead of our pilot. Two quick questions about Redwood's default hosted behavior (no Dedicated/Private yet):

1) What is the default retention window for raw request payloads (customer prompts/input)? Does that include streaming tokens and KV cache entries?
2) What is the default retention window for model-generated outputs (responses) and any derived artifacts (embeddings, summaries, reranking candidates)?
3) For EU customers: by default are these retained inside EU regions, and how does that interact with your retention/erasure workflows?

Also: can you point me to the steps to request an immediate purge or a legal hold if our compliance team asks?

Appreciate a short, actionable answer — we have a deadline next Friday.

Thanks,
Alice
Security Engineer, BrightLane

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Alice Wong <alice@brightlane.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security@brightlane.com
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 13:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify default storage for requests/outputs (EU)

Alice — thanks for the clear questions. Quick summary up-front, followed by details and action items.

Summary (short):
- Raw request payloads (prompts/inputs): default hosted retention is 14 days. Streaming token buffers are ephemeral and not persisted by default unless tracing/debug mode is enabled.
- Generated outputs (model responses): retained by default for 180 days to support debugging, evals, and quality monitoring.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks, similarity indexes): retained longer by default (365 days) because they are used for caching and similarity services; these are treated as separate artifacts.
- EU residency: by default, data for EU-tagged accounts is stored in our EU region. Deletion and purge operations target region-local stores first; cross-region backups are handled per the purge SLA below.

Details:
1) Prompts / request payloads:
   - Default window: 14 days (hosted). This includes full request bodies we capture for diagnostics.
   - Streaming tokens: the serving runtime keeps an in-memory buffer during the session; we do not persist individual token traces into long-term storage unless the customer opts into request tracing (header: x-redwood-trace: true) or enables longer retention for observability.
   - KV cache: per-session KV cache is ephemeral and not persisted beyond the session unless specifically exported by the customer.

2) Model outputs:
   - Default window: 180 days. We retain responses to support regression detection, prompt/result replay, and customer support investigations.
   - If outputs contain PII and the customer requests erasure, we follow the deletion runbook (see related_links). We mark outputs that are PII-sensitive and escalate deletion requests to the data-erase pipeline.

3) Derived artifacts:
   - Embeddings/index entries: 365 days by default. These are used by Redwood Optimize and caching layers. Customers can configure shorter windows or disable embedding persistence.

4) EU residency and erasure workflow:
   - Default: account-region mapping pins storage to EU clusters for EU-tagged organizations.
   - Erasure: hosted-account purge is performed regionally first; backups are rotated and purged within the backup retention window (details below).

5) Backups and audit logs:
   - Snapshots/backups: removed within 30 days of a purge request (we do not hold live customer data beyond the published backup rotation).
   - Audit logs required for compliance may be retained longer in anonymized form; these are scoped separately and can be redacted on request for legal erasure actions.

Options for BrightLane if you want to change defaults:
- Use the do_not_store header (x-redwood-store: never) for specific requests to avoid capture entirely.
- Upgrade to Dedicated or Private deployment to guarantee zero-hosted retention and region isolation.
- Configure per-route retention windows via the Console: short-term (7d), default (14d/180d/365d per artifact), or custom values.

I'll attach a one-pager that summarizes these defaults. If you'd like, I can schedule a quick 30-min call with our compliance engineer to walk through legal hold and erasure flows.

Attachment: redwood-retention-one-pager.pdf

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: security@brightlane.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Wong <alice@brightlane.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 08:27:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: purge SLA + backups question

Camila,

Thanks for the helpful summary. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance team:

- If we request an immediate purge (hosted account), what is the SLA for complete removal of all customer-identifying data from active stores?
- How do you handle copies in object-store snapshots and third-party backup targets (we use a strict 0-retention policy internally)?
- Is there a confirmation report you provide once deletion is complete (we need chain-of-custody evidence)?

Can you include the minimal set of steps we need to initiate an erasure and how long each step takes?

Regards,
BrightLane Security

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: security@brightlane.com
Cc: Alice Wong <alice@brightlane.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2026 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: purge SLA + backups question

Hi — here's the operational playbook and timelines for a hosted-account immediate purge. I'll also open Support Ticket #54812-BL on your behalf and link the job to the legal hold ID you provide.

Operational steps and timelines:
1) Customer request submission (you): open support ticket and provide account id + legal hold ID (same day). Estimated: <1 business day to acknowledge.
2) Scoped data identification: our data-erase team identifies all objects (requests, outputs, embeddings, attachments) tied to the account across EU region stores. Estimated: 1-2 business days.
3) Live-store deletion: we delete primary objects from active clusters. Estimated: 1 business day after identification.
4) Backup/ snapshot rotation: backups are rotated and purged within 30 calendar days; for urgent requests we can accelerate to 14 days for EU region on a best-effort basis and provide a documented exception.
5) Verification and confirmation report: we generate a deletion certificate (listing object ranges removed, timestamp, operator id). Estimated: 1 business day after deletion completion.

Notes and limitations:
- Immutable third-party archives under your control are outside Redwood's hosted scope; if you have export integrations with external storage, please include that information in the support ticket so we can coordinate.
- If you require guarantees beyond hosted policy (e.g., immediate zero-backup window), we recommend Dedicated/Private where you control retention settings and backup targets.

Action items for BrightLane:
- Reply to this thread with the account id and preferred legal-hold identifier and I'll escalate.
- If you want the accelerated 14-day backup purge commitment, please note that in the ticket and we'll include the exception in the deletion certificate.

I'll loop in our Data Erase lead (marissa_cole) for execution.

Best regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
